cf.title: Fix timeline history after recovery stops on an ancestor

input.subject: [PATCH] Fix timeline history after recovery stops on an ancestor

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The problem is stated with a reproducible scenario in message #1, and the new parent matches the PrevTimeLineID that the end-of-recovery record already uses. Three reviewers agree on lastRecTLI as the parent. The open points are the back-patch decision and the empty v2 commit message, and both belong to the committer.

brief.title: Use last replayed timeline as parent in new timeline history file
brief.problem: When recovery with recovery_target_timeline = 'latest' stops at a target on timeline 1 before timeline 2 forked, Postgres writes timeline 2 as the parent of the new timeline. The resulting history file lists switchpoints that go backwards, so tools that walk timeline history, such as a WAL verifier, cannot rebuild the real ancestry.
brief.proposed_design: writeTimeLineHistory() takes the timeline of the last replayed WAL record (lastRecTLI) as the parent instead of recoveryTargetTLI. The new timeline ID is still chosen from the newest timeline in the archive. 028_pitr_timelines.pl now checks the history file content, and 002_archiving.pl replays WAL on timeline 2 and waits for it before promotion.
user_visible_surface: Content of the timeline history file written at end of archive recovery: the parent timeline and switchpoint change when recovery stops on an ancestor timeline.
author_claims: The current history file does not describe the timeline switches that took place.
The bug is a correctness issue and the fix should be back-patched.
The new parent matches the PrevTimeLineID that the end-of-recovery record already uses.
brief.thread_state: Andrey Rachitskiy, Andrey Borodin and João Rito agree that lastRecTLI is the right parent; v2 fixed a race in 002_archiving.pl that Borodin found. Rito tested master and back branches and would mark it Ready for Committer once the commit message is rewritten; Heikki and Michael were asked to comment but have not replied.
unclear: No case is shown where the wrong history file breaks pg_rewind, standby timeline choice or any other tool, which matters for the back-patch decision.
The v2 commit message has a one-line subject and an empty body.
The thread does not say how existing clusters with a wrong history file should be handled, or whether release notes should mention it.
The thread does not say whether any code path depends on the old parent value.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: The parent timeline and switchpoint written to a new timeline history file change; the file format stays the same.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: The change is in the end-of-archive-recovery path in xlog.c and affects the history file that standbys and archive tools read.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The author asks for a back-patch, which changes history file content in minor releases without a demonstrated broken consumer.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Which concrete tool or server path (pg_rewind, standby timeline choice, an archive tool) misbehaves today with the wrong history file, to justify a back-patch?
Does any code path or external tool depend on the old parent value, or on promotion restoring the target timeline's history file from the archive?
What should users do with clusters and archives that already hold a history file with backward switchpoints, and should the release notes say so?
Is there a case where recovery ends with lastRecTLI different from recoveryTargetTLI and recoveryTargetTLI is still the correct parent?
Can the v2 commit message be rewritten to explain the scenario, the choice of lastRecTLI over endOfLogTLI, and the test changes?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows the end-of-recovery and timeline switch code in xlog.c; message #2 asked Heikki and Michael to comment, and neither has replied in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The committer signs for the content of history files written at end of archive recovery in every branch that receives the fix, including any effect on tools that read the old content. History files stay in archives for a long time.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v2 with a fix for the race in 002_archiving.pl that message #3 reported, which shows a response to review.

priority.reason: The fix is a 3.8 KB patch to one call in xlog.c plus two tests, and it affects only PITR that stops on an ancestor timeline. Reviewers agree on the design, but no committer who knows the area has replied.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so it is not confirmed that lastRecTLI is always valid when writeTimeLineHistory() runs, or that no other path reads the old parent. The two linked discussions in message #1 were also not available.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: get current and recovery timeline
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set out to let tools read the current timeline of a standby from shared memory, first by allowing pg_walfile_name() on a standby and later through new functions that return the LSN and timeline together. The last version changed pg_stat_get_wal_receiver() to return the last known values when no WAL receiver runs, and added applied_lsn and applied_tli columns.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier objected to the last version because pg_stat_wal_receiver maps one to one to the shared memory state of a running WAL receiver, and applied WAL belongs to the startup process. He also did not want to change the check that returns NULL when no WAL receiver is ready, on security grounds. He suggested a separate view over XLogCtl, such as pg_stat_recovery, and returned the patch at the end of the CF.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
pg_stat_wal_receiver is just a one-one mapping with the shared memory
state of the WAL receiver itself and show data *if and only if* a WAL
receiver is running and iff it is ready to display any data, so I'd
rather not change its nature and it has nothing to do with the state
of WAL being applied by the startup process.  So this gets a -1 from
me.

precedents_retrieved.title: Archive current timeline history file on archiver startup if needed
precedents_retrieved.summary: When a primary on a timeline above 1 has WAL archiving enabled after its last timeline switch, the history file for its current timeline is never archived. This breaks cascading standbys and explicit-timeline PITR built from `-X none` base backups. The patch proposed archiving that history file if it is not yet archived, first at archiver startup and later at the end of StartupXLOG, with an alternative patch letting recovery proceed when the initial timeline's history file cannot be fetched.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Kyotaro Horiguchi objected to archiving the same file repeatedly. Robert Haas rejected the alternative of fetching the history file and ignoring errors, and asked whether the two patches were alternatives. After Robert Haas's review the author did not reply, the entry was set to Waiting on Author, and it was later returned with feedback because the feedback had not been addressed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It seems to me that trying to fetch a timeline history file and then
ignoring any error has got to be wrong.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow PostgreSQL to perform promote/pause/shutdown operations at end-of-the-wal when the recovery does not reach the recovery target
precedents_retrieved.summary: The proposal stops recovery from promoting at the end of available WAL when the recovery target was not reached, with a new setting (recovery_target_incomplete) to promote, pause or shut down instead. It later split into a second patch that refuses to start WAL replay when the recovery target lies before the restored backup's position, checked against pg_control.
precedents_retrieved.objection: David Steele found the start-point check incorrect: it uses the checkpoint in pg_control, but backup recovery starts from the backup_label checkpoint, and PITR can only start at backup end. The check would accept invalid targets in long backups and reject valid ones, and the last completed xid says little about commit order. He also noted that no consensus existed for the behaviour change, and returned the patch at the end of the CF.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
My point is that the
information you are working from (whatever checkpoint happens to be in
pg_control when recovery starts) is not sufficient for the task.  This
method is inaccurate and would disallow valid recovery scenarios.

precedents_retrieved.title: New argument "latest" for recovery_target parameter
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a value "latest" for recovery_target that makes recovery apply all available WAL explicitly, so recovery_target_action takes effect and backup tools can detect conflicting targets. Later versions also defined end of WAL for standbys by changing WaitForWALToBecomeAvailable to return when the archive, pg_wal and streaming sources were exhausted.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tomas Vondra returned the patch because it had been waiting on the author with no update since early December, after Kyotaro Horiguchi's review of the 2019-12-08 version. Peter Eisentraut supported making the existing default behavior explicit, but said a new end-of-WAL behavior for standbys needed a separate discussion, and he disliked the name "latest".
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
this patch was waiting on author without any update/response since early
December, so I've marked it as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Creating backup history files for backups taken from standbys
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pg_stop_backup write a backup history file for backups taken on a standby, as it already does on a primary, so a standby with archive_mode = always can archive it. A later version writes the file only when archiving is active for the mode in which the backup started.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Fujii Masao pointed out that all backups taken on a standby before the next restartpoint share the same start point, so they produce backup history files with the same name and different content. The author then noted that archive commands such as a plain cp fail on these duplicate names, which makes WAL pile up on the standby. Neither the alternatives (adding the file to the base backup, or renaming it) was judged worth the work in the last CF, so the author dropped the patch and David Steele agreed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Something I did not consider though is that this causes archive commands to choke on those identical file names, so any archive command which is not able to handle that would cause WAL to bloat on the standby.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow subfield references without parentheses
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets column references with three or more identifiers be read as a correlation name, a column and one or more composite-type fields, as the SQL standard allows, so `A.B.C` can mean `(A.B).C`. The correlation must be an explicit alias, and the parser raises an error when both readings apply.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Tom Lane raised possible new ambiguity but agreed with raising an error, and Ashutosh Bapat suggested building the reference through transformIndirection(). The patch also still had TODOs for documentation and for SQL and PL/pgSQL parameters, and no reply after 2024-12-13 is shown.

precedents_retrieved.title: history of vacuum / checkpoint runs
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add hooks that run after vacuum and checkpoint logging, and keep a history of individual runs that users can query instead of parsing the server log. A proof-of-concept extension stored events in a fixed-size circular buffer in shared memory, and the discussion moved toward a file with a time-based retention limit.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Reviewers discussed buffer size, file storage, retention policy, hook signatures and aggregation, but none of the shown messages objects to the idea. The last shown message is from January 2025 and the entry was withdrawn in November 2025, with no visible reason.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert recent changes with durable_rename_excl()
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert recent changes with durable_rename_excl()
Reverted commit(s): Remove durable_rename_excl(); Replace existing durable_rename_excl() calls with durable_rename()
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commits 2c902bb and ccfbd92.  Per buildfarm members
kestrel, rorqual and calliphoridae, the assertions checking that a TLI
history file should not exist when created by a WAL receiver have been
failing, and switching to durable_rename() over durable_rename_excl()
would cause the newest TLI history file to overwrite the existing one.
We need to think harder about such cases, so revert the new logic for
now.

Note that all the failures have been reported in the test
025_stuck_on_old_timeline.

precedents_retrieved.title: Extend pgbench partitioning to pgbench_history
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pgbench's --partitions option also partition pgbench_history, using the same method as pgbench_accounts. It adds no separate option to turn this on or off.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author did not answer Melanie Plageman's review for about three months, so Robert Haas returned the entry with feedback. She asked why the history table should be partitioned by account ID rather than by time, and why tellers and branches were left out. She also said the doc text wrongly implies that the pgbench_history partitions are created with equal sizes.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Since there has been no response to these review comments for more
than 3 months, I have set https://commitfest.postgresql.org/48/4679/
to Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.summary:
Add more TAP coverage for archive status with crash recovery of standbys

precedents_retrieved.objection:
This part of the test was included originally in 4e87c48, but got
reverted as of f9c1b8d because of timing issues in the test, where,
after more analysis, we found that the standbys may not have recovered
from the archives all the segments needed by the test.  This stabilizes
the test by making sure that standbys replay up to the position returned
by pg_switch_wal(), meaning that all segments are recovered before the
manual checkpoint that tests WAL segment recycling and its interactions
with archive status files.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P11] concerns pg_rewind and diverging timelines, a different idea, and records no reason that could apply here. Messages #1 and #2 link two related discussions, but the material does not say what they concluded, so nothing from them is carried over.

From the standards and compatibility angle there is nothing to reject: no new syntax, GUC, catalog object, dump content, psql surface or protocol change. The only user-visible change is the parent timeline and switchpoint in a history file written once at end of archive recovery, and only in a case where the current content is self-contradictory. Every other consumer, such as the end-of-recovery record's PrevTimeLineID, already uses lastRecTLI (message #2, message #6). One effect is visible in the tests: a promoted standby that never replayed timeline 2 no longer restores 00000002.history from the archive (message #6, comment 3). That narrows archive reads and breaks no documented contract. The thread shows no tool that depends on the old parent value, and inventing one would break the rubric's no-invented-facts guard. Open points remain for the committer, not for rejection: back-patching a change to a minor release's history file content without a demonstrated failure (message #6, comment 4), and a release-note line for clusters that already carry such a file. [P11] concerns pg_rewind and diverging timelines, has no recorded reason, and does not support an objection here.

The only persistent state touched is the parent and switchpoint lines that a new timeline history file records; the file format, WAL records, control file and catalogs stay the same. The new parent matches the PrevTimeLineID already written to the end-of-recovery record, so on-disk state becomes consistent. Existing wrong history files are left as they are and are not made worse. The new timeline ID is still chosen from the archive, so later promotions cannot reuse an ID. A back-patch changes no format that mixed-version standbys read. [P11] concerns pg_rewind and records no reason, so it does not apply. The thread shows no case where pg_rewind or a standby's timeline choice depends on the old parent value; that cannot be checked without the code.

The proposal changes only the parent timeline that the server writes into a history file at the end of archive recovery. It adds no new privilege, SQL surface, setting or exposure, and no unprivileged user can reach or influence this path, so there is no security angle to review.

From the maintenance and fit angle there is nothing to object to. The patch changes the parent argument of one existing writeTimeLineHistory() call so that it matches the PrevTimeLineID already written to the end-of-recovery record. It adds no GUC, catalog change, API, dependency or hot-path work, and later features have no new place to update. The bug belongs in core because the history file is a core format. Three reviewers agree on the design (messages #2, #3, #6). Committability: the committers who know this area were asked in message #2 and have not replied. The back-patch case would be stronger with a concrete broken consumer, which message #6 asks for. One candidate from general knowledge: a standby on timeline 1 between A and B may follow timeline 3 because the wrong file shows timeline 1 valid until B. The patch also changes promotion so that it no longer restores the target timeline's history file from the archive, as message #6 shows for 002_archiving.pl. External archive tools that expect that file could notice this, but the material shows no such tool. [P11] is about pg_rewind and has no recorded reason, so it does not apply.

This is a bug fix to the content of the history file that core writes at end of recovery. No existing feature, option or extension can make core write a correct parent timeline, so the already-exists angle has nothing to raise. [P11] is about pg_rewind and diverging timelines, and no reason is recorded for it, so it does not apply.

This is a small correctness fix with no ongoing cost and no new user surface. It also makes the history file agree with the PrevTimeLineID that the end-of-recovery record already uses. Message #6 asks for user-visible impact, but that only decides whether to back-patch, not whether to fix master, and I found no concrete failure scenario to support a demand objection.
